title: The Sahara Desert Secretly Feeds the Amazon Rainforest

scenes.text: The Sahara Desert feeds the Amazon rainforest. Every single year.
Every year, winds blow Saharan dust 1,600 miles across the Atlantic. About 27 million tons of it lands on the Amazon.
That's enough dust to fill over a hundred thousand semi trucks.
Hidden inside it is phosphorus, a fertilizer the rainforest badly needs, because heavy rain keeps washing it out of the soil.
Much of it comes from one dried-up ancient lake in Chad, packed with the remains of tiny organisms rich in phosphorus.
NASA tracked the dust from space for seven years, and what it delivers roughly matches what the rain washes away.
So the biggest hot desert on Earth keeps the biggest rainforest alive. What else is secretly connected?

description:
The Sahara Desert feeds the Amazon rainforest, every single year.
NASA's CALIPSO satellite tracked about 182 million tons of dust leaving the Sahara each year; around 27.7 million tons land on the Amazon, carrying roughly 22,000 tons of phosphorus, about what the rain washes out of the forest's soil.
What else on this planet do you think is secretly connected?
